item.title: Chip substrate makers face 30-month waits for key equipment
item.description: Delivery times for some equipment used to manufacture advanced chip substrates have stretched from six months to 30 months as manufacturers race to expand production to meet surging demand for artificial intelligence (AI) chips.
item.dc:creator: DIGITIMES

media:content.media:description: Ushio's lithography equipment for advanced IC package substrates. Credit: Ushio

item.title: Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix strike multiyear memory deals
item.description: The world's three largest memory chipmakers are securing multiyear supply agreements as shortages driven by AI demand push customers to commit cash years before chips are delivered.
item.dc:creator: DIGITIMES

item.title: Nvidia reportedly halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries as new US chip rule bites
item.description: Nvidia has told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, the Financial Times (FT) reported on November 26, as a new US rule against Chinese companies' rented access to AI computing hits the region's data center boom and governments there race to show Washington they will comply.
item.dc:creator: DIGITIMES

item.title: CBTech launches TGV foundry production line, secures sample orders from 5 major customers
item.description: Precision exposure equipment maker Chime Ball Technology (CBTech) announced on November 25 that Taiwan's first full-process foundry production line for through glass via (TGV) and glass core substrates (GCS) has been completed and has begun operations at its headquarters in Luzhu, Taoyuan.
item.dc:creator: Eifeh Strom

media:content.media:description: CBTech Chairman Hung-Ming Chang. Credit: CBTech

item.title: Intel lawsuit details Trump's push for US$8.9 billion stake
item.description: A US Commerce Department lawyer warned Intel's management in August 2025 against treating a proposed government equity stake as a negotiation, according to internal company records cited in a shareholder lawsuit and reported by Wired.
item.dc:creator: DIGITIMES
